newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest power mostly steady, SPP moves higher.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest power mostly steady, SPP moves higher.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the midwestern U.S. were mostly steady Wednesday although short-term SPP prices moved higher with some below normal temperatures expected, the brokers and marketers said.
In the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP), Thursday peak, non-firm power prices were pegged steady at $16.50-18.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), the brokers and marketers said.
MAPP temperatures were forecast to rise to above normal as the weekend approaches and reach well above normal levels before the end of the weekend.
Off-peak non-firm MAPP next day power was said to be unchanged at $11.00-13.00.
In the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN), peak, non-firm power prices for Thursday were assessed steady at $16.50-17.50, the sources said.
Temperatures in MAIN were expected to be above normal Thursday and Friday, then cool to near normal for Saturday, and return to above normal levels for Sunday and Monday.
MAIN off peak next day power was said to be steady at $11.00-13.00 per MWh.

Peak, non-firm electricity prices in the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR) for Thursday were said to be discussed slightly higher at $16.00-18.00 from $15.00-17.50 on Tuesday, the sources said.
Temperatures in ECAR were expected to be above normal through Friday, then cool for Saturday.
ECAR electricity prices for off-peak, non-firm next day delivery were notionally assessed steady at $12.00-14.00 per MWh.
March ECAR was said to be talked steady at $20.20-20.75 per MWh.

In the Southwest Power Pool (SPP) peak, non-firm power prices for Thursday delivery were pegged higher at $19.00-21.00 from $17.50-19.50, while in the south next day peak power was assessed at $17.00-19.00 from $15.50-16.50 on Tuesday.
Off-peak non-firm next day prices throughout SPP were assessed higher at $12.00-14.00 from $10.50-12.50 on Tuesday, the sources said.
In SPP, temperatures were forecast to be normal to just below normal Thursday, then rise to one to five degrees above normal through the weekend.
March peak SPP was talked at $19.95-20.30 from $20.15-20.35 per MWh on Tuesday.
